html:
The Winnimem Wintu, "middle water people", are a Wintu people of the McCloud River in northern California, north of today's Redding. They lived in villages along the river, and salmon was the centre of their lives and ceremonies. Related groups include the Northern Wintu and Dau Pom, and their northern neighbours were the Shasta.

After the Gold Rush miners and settlers took the land, and many Winnimem were killed. In 1872 the US Fish Commission set up a hatchery on the McCloud, and salmon eggs from the river were shipped around the world, including to New Zealand. In 1945 Shasta Dam flooded their villages and burial grounds and blocked the salmon.

The Winnimem are not recognised by the US government. Under their leader Caleen Sisk they campaign to bring the salmon home, using fish descended from those sent to New Zealand.
